documents.unit: Academic Honor Code (Academic Catalog, Office of the Provost)
documents.title: The Academic Honor Code
documents.summary: The Academic Honor Code defines AI use that breaks instructor or university guidelines, or is not expressly permitted by the instructor, as cheating. It sets no AI rule of its own: whether and how AI is allowed varies by course and is the instructor's call, and students must check with the instructor and keep up with changing guidelines. The rest of the code (procedures, appeals) is general and not AI-specific.
documents.stance_why: Section III.H says "How and whether instructors permit the use of AI products will vary widely from course to course, and is always subject to each instructor's authority and guidelines", so the document sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors (delegates), while backing it with a fallback ban on AI "not expressly permitted by the instructor". No tiers or templates are offered.

units.why: The cheating definition says cheating "also consists of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) products in a way that violates an instructor's guidelines"; it classifies improper AI use as misconduct, so it is a P36 rule binding students at the point of misuse (when-misuse), stated as a prohibition.
units.anchor: use of artificial intelligence (AI) products in a way that violates an instructor’s guidelines

units.why: The same sentence adds "or using it to complete coursework in a way not expressly permitted by the instructor", so AI is off unless the instructor expressly permits it. This is the fallback rule (P06), not P36, because it sets the default when instructors have said nothing.
units.anchor: using it to complete coursework in a way not expressly permitted by the instructor

units.why: The cheating paragraph says "It is the responsibility of the student to consult with the instructor concerning what constitutes permissible collaboration and what materials/products are allowed"; it tells students to ask the instructor what is allowed, which is P10. It speaks of materials/products, so AI is covered only by reference to the preceding AI sentence.
units.anchor: responsibility of the student to consult with the instructor concerning what constitutes permissible collaboration
units.frag_start: It is the responsibility of the
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific wording: covers collaboration and any materials or products, with AI implied by the preceding sentence.

units.why: Section III.H states "Use of technology (including AI) in a way that violates instructor and/or University guidelines ... is prohibited"; it makes violating AI guidelines a standalone honor-code violation, so P36 (misconduct) with a must-not modality, not P01 since it bans only non-compliant use.
units.anchor: Use of technology (including AI) in a way that violates instructor and/or University guidelines

units.why: III.H says "How and whether instructors permit the use of AI products will vary widely from course to course, and is always subject to each instructor's authority"; the university sets no AI rule itself and hands the decision to instructors, which is P04.
units.anchor: How and whether instructors permit the use of AI products will vary widely

units.why: III.H instructs "Students should always check with the instructor before using these products to complete their coursework"; students unsure of what is allowed ask first, so P10 with a should modality.
units.anchor: Students should always check with the instructor before using these products

units.why: III.H warns "Guidelines about these practices may change over time, so students should be sure to ask for the most up-to-date guidelines"; it asks students to keep current with changing guidance (P102) rather than describing a review cycle (P54). The policy is also acknowledged as provisional.
units.anchor: Guidelines about these practices may change over time, so students should be sure to ask
units.fit_note: Also acknowledges that AI guidelines change over time (P54) but does not commit to a review cycle.

units.why: III.H ends "For broader University level guidance please refer to" the UDit AI policies page; it points students to a separate university guidance document. No type fits well: it is not a framework (P56) or a statement of rules, only a referral.
units.anchor: For broader University level guidance please refer to
units.uncovered_note: Refers students to a separate university-level AI guidance page (login-protected) for broader rules.

notes: Only one included document. Coded only AI-related passages; general honor-code text (pledge, other conduct standards, sanctions, report and appeal procedures in IV-VI) was skipped because it never mentions AI, though it governs AI cases too. The linked UDit AI guidance requires login and was not available.
